Macro tone from the May 2019 FOMC statement is mildly positive (strong labor market, solid activity, patient stance amid muted inflation). However, the April 2019 SLOOS points to emerging credit headwinds: banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and tightened other terms across firm sizes; demand weakened for construction/land development, HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans, with auto and subprime mortgage demand roughly unchanged. These tighter standards and softer loan demand suggest a more cautious outlook than a purely macro read, aligning with the financial stability concerns around elevated corporate leverage and stretched valuations. Net: still slightly positive, but trimmed by credit tightening and weaker demand.
